comments.body: Well, we'd need to reproduce it somehow. It's possible the HLO will suffice to reproduce it, so we could certainly try that? Can you share an HLO dump? (Set `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_dump_to=/somewhere` and zip up `/somewhere` and attach it to the issue.)

I've been running into a similar (or the same?) issue, where my Python script would crash with an `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`. I've managed to simplify my code by quite a lot, and have gotten to the following MWE:

```python
# mwe.py
from jax import jit
import jax.numpy as jnp

@jit
def test(b: jnp.ndarray, d: jnp.ndarray):
    return d.at[b[:,0]].set(1, mode="drop")

SIZE_B = 2500
SIZE_C = 6000**2

b = jnp.zeros(SIZE_B**2, dtype=jnp.int32).reshape((SIZE_B,SIZE_B))
c = jnp.zeros(SIZE_C)
d = jnp.zeros(1, dtype=jnp.int32)

e = test(b, d)
```

Removing the JIT annotation or changing the order of allocations in any way seems to cause the error to disappear, as does making either SIZE_B or SIZE_C much smaller. Furthermore, it also requires the environment variable `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR` to be set to `platform`.

Running this script gives me the following output:

```
$ XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=platform python ./mwe.py
E0224 17:35:32.278683   15179 cuda_executor.cc:498] failed to free device memory at 0x79448d602600; result: INTERNAL: CUDA error: : CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS: an illegal memory access was encountered
E0224 17:35:32.278703   15179 pjrt_stream_executor_client.cc:3045] Execution of replica 0 failed: INTERNAL: Failed to complete all kernels launched on stream 0x256f6330: CUDA error: Could not synchronize CUDA stream: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS: an illegal memory access was encountered
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "~/jax_repro/./mwe.py", line 15, in <module>
    e = test(b, d)
        ^^^^^^^^^^
jaxlib.xla_extension.XlaRuntimeError: INTERNAL: Failed to complete all kernels launched on stream 0x256f6330: CUDA error: Could not synchronize CUDA stream: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS: an illegal memory access was encountered
--------------------
For simplicity, JAX has removed its internal frames from the traceback of the following exception. Set JAX_TRACEBACK_FILTERING=off to include these.
E0224 17:35:32.282557   15179 cuda_executor.cc:248] failed to unload module 0x25b57fe0; leaking: INTERNAL: CUDA error: : CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS: an illegal memory access was encountered
... (similar errors trimmed)
```

I've tested this on three different GPUs, an A4000-Ada, A5000-Ada and an RTX 3080 Mobile. This was tested on JAX version 0.5.0, with Python version 3.12.3 and 3.12.8 on Linux. If you want any more details, feel free to let me know.

EDIT: I've simplified the MWE slightly.

I've spent a bit of time digging into the generated LLVM IR (found using `--xla_dump_to=./xla_dump`). The LLVM IR for the `test` function is as follows:

```llvm
; ModuleID = 'jit_test'
source_filename = "jit_test"
target datalayout = "e-i64:64-i128:128-v16:16-v32:32-n16:32:64"
target triple = "nvptx64-nvidia-cuda"

; Function Attrs: mustprogress nofree norecurse nosync nounwind willreturn memory(argmem: readwrite)
define void @input_scatter_fusion(ptr noalias nocapture writeonly align 128 dereferenceable(8) %0, ptr noalias nocapture readonly align 16 dereferenceable(25000000) %1) local_unnamed_addr #0 {
  %3 = addrspacecast ptr %1 to ptr addrspace(1)
  %4 = addrspacecast ptr %0 to ptr addrspace(1)
  %5 = tail call i32 @llvm.nvvm.read.ptx.sreg.tid.x(), !range !4
  %6 = tail call i32 @llvm.nvvm.read.ptx.sreg.ctaid.x(), !range !5
  %7 = mul nuw nsw i32 %5, 2500
  %8 = mul nuw nsw i32 %6, 320000
  %9 = add nuw nsw i32 %7, %8
  %10 = zext nneg i32 %9 to i64
  %11 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %3, i64 %10
  %12 = load i32, ptr addrspace(1) %11, align 16, !invariant.load !6
  %13 = lshr i32 %12, 30
  %14 = and i32 %13, 2
  %15 = add i32 %14, %12
  %16 = icmp ult i32 %15, 2
  %17 = shl nuw nsw i32 %6, 7
  %18 = or disjoint i32 %17, %5
  %19 = icmp samesign ult i32 %18, 2500
  %or.cond = and i1 %19, %16
  %20 = zext nneg i32 %15 to i64
  %21 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %4, i64 %20
  br i1 %or.cond, label %22, label %23

22:                                               ; preds = %2
  store atomic i32 1, ptr addrspace(1) %21 unordered, align 4
  br label %23

23:                                               ; preds = %22, %2
  ret void
}
```

If you look at the load for `%12`, you can see that no bounds checking is being done for the index. `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` supports this, as this gives the following output:

```
========= Invalid __global__ read of size 4 bytes
=========     at input_scatter_fusion+0x80
=========     by thread (96,0,0) in block (19,0,0)
=========     Address 0x7326f181be00 is out of bounds
=========     and is 280,001 bytes after the nearest allocation at 0x7326f0000000 of size 25,000,000 bytes
```

Calculating the value for `%9`, we find an index of 6320000, 70000 past the last index of `b` (`%1`), which matches the out of bounds address exactly (280,001 bytes = 70000 elements). Therefore, it seems there is a bug somewhere in the codegen, which accidentally removes the boundscheck.
Can you please also post the HLO before optimizations here that was dumped?
Just verified it using JAX 0.5.3, it should be fixed now.

issue.body:
Dear developers,

We are trying to intergrate recovar into Scipion. I've got two servers. 

Server A
- GTX 1080Ti (11G), RTX 2080Ti (11G) and 4500Ada (24G).
- Ubuntu 24.04LTS, gcc-12, miniforge3

Server B
- Tesla T4 (16G)
- Ubuntu 22.04LTS, gcc-12, miniforge3

We tried to install recovar+cryodrgn as per the instructions in the main GitHub page, and then running "recovar run_test_dataset". On server A all tests pass. On server B, however, none of them pass.

In both cases, there is +500GB free on the root disk, and no one is using the GPUs. I'm attaching the error from server B. It's full of messages about illegal memory accesses after XLA compilation of some CUDA kernels. Any idea on why the vanilla installation fails on B but not on A?

Thanks in advance,
M. Iceta, BioComputing Unit CNB-CSIC

[recovar_error.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19409677/recovar_error.txt)
